latest_rss.title: Translation: The Deluge of Blocked Words Online – Why We Feel We “Cannot Speak Openly”
latest_rss.summary:
The post translated below, from WeChat account “Summer Flavors,” argues that keyword-based censorship on Chinese online platforms is missing the mark, both unnecessarily restricting harmless speech and failing to address the problems it is meant to target. This leaves users struggling to articulate even relatively innocuous messages in ways that will survive. The post carefully frames intense current restrictions as a product of blunt management by the platforms themselves. Depoliticising the issue like this might appear questionable, and blaming the platforms might seem like shooting the messenger, but companies do have leeway in how they fulfil their entwined legal and political duties. These choices determine how most users will actually experience censorship, and can be challenged in ways that other aspects of the censorship regime cannot. The post currently remains online.
